record.title: TAIS-Net: Time adaptive implicit sampling diffusion model for arbitrary-scale UAV video super-resolution
record.abstract: Emerging applications urgently require unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) videos with high clarity and rich structural details. However, limitations in imaging sensors and non-ideal conditions often result in blurred videos lacking sufficient details. Recent studies indicate diffusion models have strong potential for natural scene video super-resolution (SR). However, the application of diffusion models to UAV video SR remains underexplored, particularly in the context of arbitrary-scale reconstruction. To tackle the challenges in UAV video SR at arbitrary scales, this work introduces a time adaptive implicit sampling diffusion model TAIS-Net. First, to achieve robust temporal alignment under large camera motions and texture scarcity commonly encountered in UAV videos, we use a reference frame alignment module to compensate previously reconstructed frames by incorporating motion cues estimated from a pre-trained optical flow model. Second, to enable scale-flexible reconstruction while preserving fine geometric details for UAV videos under arbitrary upscaling factors, we introduce an implicit denoising U-Net to learn latent features by leveraging implicit neural representations and a temporal conditioning module. Third, to reduce the prediction error propagation during sampling, we introduce a historical sample gain module that dynamically corrects and refines latent features at each sampling step, thereby suppressing temporal artifacts such as flickering or drifting. Finally, an arbitrary-scale implicit decoder is used to reconstruct high-resolution videos directly from these enhanced latent features, avoiding scale-dependent blurring while preserving high-frequency details in UAV videos. To validate the effectiveness of TAIS-Net, we construct two visible and one infrared UAV video SR datasets. The experimental results on these datasets demonstrate that TAIS-Net attains competitive performance relative to existing methods in terms of reconstruction quality, perceptual quality and temporal consistency. Moreover, experiments on various motion intensities and additional Gaussian blur beyond conventional bicubic downsampling degradation without requiring model retraining also demonstrate the superiority of our TAIS-Net in maintaining perceptual and temporal consistency under real-world UAV scenarios. The code and datasets are available at https://github.com/cyber-lwk/TAIS-Net.

record.title: Shallow-water reef detection driven by few-shot learning with airborne LiDAR bathymetry
record.abstract: Shallow-water reefs play an important scientific and practical role in ensuring navigational safety and supporting marine aquaculture. However, traditional detection methods such as shipborne sonar and multibeam echo sounding face significant challenges in achieving high-precision detection. These challenges stem from complex reef morphology and grounding risks associated with unmanned surface vehicles. In contrast, airborne LiDAR bathymetry (ALB) provides an effective alternative, enabling non-contact, high-accuracy measurements over broad spatial extents. This study proposes a few-shot learning–based detection method using ALB data. It addresses challenges posed by large morphological variability and limited training samples in shallow-water reef detection. We developed upon an enhanced You Only Look Once version 10 (YOLOv10) framework, incorporating a Cross-Scale Attention Module (CSAM) to strengthen feature perception and representation. Moreover, a joint training strategy is employed to enhance model adaptability. This strategy integrates data augmentation with meta-learning to ensure robustness under few-shot scenarios. The proposed approach was validated using ALB data collected over Jiaozhou Bay, Qingdao, China. Experimental results under few-shot conditions (10 samples) show that the proposed method achieves a precision of 97.9% and a recall of 98.4%, demonstrating superior detection accuracy and stability compared with existing algorithms. These findings establish a reliable technical foundation for high-precision shallow-water reef detection in marine engineering and environmental monitoring applications. For benchmarking and reproducibility purposes, the constructed ReefFeat-Img dataset and the source code of the proposed method are publicly available at: https://github.com/biguanglu350/FSAM-YOLO.git.

record.title: Sparse multimodal feature fusion transformer with frequency-convolution collaboration for wildlife multi-object tracking in UAV monitoring
record.abstract: Lightweight unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are gradually becoming important remote sensing tools for wildlife monitoring. Wildlife tracking using UAVs faces challenges, including small targets, highly similar appearances, and strong camouflage in natural environments. To address these issues, we propose a multimodal wildlife multi-object tracking model based on text–image feature fusion. First, the Density Multimodal Fusion (DTF) module combines spatial-density-guided sparse sampling with text priors to focus on high-density foregrounds while suppressing background redundancy. Second, the frequency-convolution collaborative encoder (LST-Encoder) performs spatially conditioned spectral modulation to enhance informative frequency components and preserve global semantics, improving discriminability for camouflaged and visually similar targets. Finally, the Hybrid-Decoder mitigates ID switches and identity fragmentation by integrating global spatiotemporal modeling with hierarchical identity modulation, maintaining cross-frame feature continuity and reinforcing identity-specific cues for stable long-sequence tracking. We validate our approach on the newly constructed MiluDrone dataset and public datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed method significantly outperforms several representative trackers, achieving a 4% increase in MOTA, a 3.7% increase in IDF1, and a 47% reduction in ID switches on the MiluDrone dataset. These results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed framework for challenging UAV-based wildlife monitoring scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/yzxhao123/De-MOTR.git.

record.title: Deviation-guided dual-model machine learning SAR coherence change detection framework for extracting changes in low-coherence areas
record.abstract: Coherence Change Detection (CCD) is a crucial technique for monitoring surface dynamics in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), and it has wide-ranging applications in natural disaster monitoring and urban analysis. However, conventional CCD methods based on dual-temporal coherence typically rely on a single coherence estimate for decision-making. This makes it difficult to effectively distinguish between decoherence caused by real surface changes and that induced by other factors, such as geometric decorrelation, temporal decorrelation, system noise, and co-registration inaccuracies. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel dual-model framework for coherence change detection that integrates machine learning with coherence and deviation modeling. The proposed framework first employs a machine learning (ML) model for coherence estimation, followed by a deviation prediction model that learns the mapping between statistical features and estimation errors. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method is then applied to interpret the deviation model. Based on the joint output of coherence and deviation estimates, a dual-threshold segmentation strategy is adopted to effectively extract low-coherence regions caused by genuine surface changes. Experimental results confirm the method’s robustness in small-sample and low-coherence scenarios. Validation with real-world data across different resolutions and scenarios confirms the method’s ability to accurately identify low-coherence regions caused by changes. By jointly utilizing coherence and deviation information, the proposed framework enhances detection accuracy and interpretability, providing a robust and reliable new CCD solution.

record.title: Multimodal deep learning with aerial imagery and nDSM for true-slope-aware rooftop photovoltaic potential estimation
record.abstract: Accurate assessment of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) potential is essential for renewable energy planning and carbon-neutral urban development. Most existing studies rely on a single data modality: aerial image-based methods often lack true-slope information, while three-dimensional (3D) building model-based methods usually omit roof superstructures and their impact on installable area. These limitations can introduce systematic errors and lead to biased PV potential estimates. To address these challenges, we propose SolarFusion, an innovative multimodal deep learning framework for high-precision, true-slope-aware rooftop PV potential assessment. SolarFusion combines semantic features from RGB aerial imagery with geometric-spatial attributes from normalized digital surface model (nDSM) data. At its core is the FusionPIRNet architecture, which integrates the cross-modal multi-scale feature integration (CMFI) module for adaptive coupling of heterogeneous data and the continual fusion optimization (CFO) module for progressive refinement of fused features. Two high-quality RGB-D benchmark datasets, RID1-Depth (0.10 m/pixel nDSM) and RID2-Depth (0.08 m/pixel nDSM), are constructed to enable robust evaluation and introduce true-slope awareness into rooftop PV analysis. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SolarFusion outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal fusion methods in both rooftop parsing and PV potential estimation. In particular, SolarFusion achieves the lowest estimation error, reducing the annual solar potential estimation error by at least 98.85 MWh/year on RID1-Depth and 44.61 MWh/year on RID2-Depth. A city-wide case study in Munich, Germany (374 km2) further highlights the framework’s scalability, identifying an annual generation potential of 3.2 TWh and successfully handling diverse urban morphologies, including high-density districts with complex rooftop configurations.

record.title: Towards comprehensive multi-task land cover change detection leveraging vision-language model and LLM-driven agents
record.abstract: Land cover change detection is essential for assessing the impacts of urbanization on ecological systems and economic development. As urbanization accelerates, land cover changes involve both semantic transitions and structural modifications, substantially increasing the complexity of detection tasks. However, existing research has primarily focused on 2D change detection, with limited integration of multi-dimensional and multi-modal data. This limitation has restricted the effective modeling of inter-class transitions and spatial structural evolution. Moreover, most methods lack end-to-end pipelines adapted to real-world scenarios, constraining their capacity for comprehensive representation and quantitative impact assessment. To address these challenges, we introduce UrbanChange, the first dataset designed for multi-task (2D and 3D) land cover change detection. It integrates semantic and structural change maps from multi-sensor data with fine-grained change captions, providing a comprehensive foundation for evaluating and analyzing land cover transformations. Leveraging UrbanChange, we develop a vision–language model that directly infers multi-dimensional changes from optical imagery. We further develop GaiaAgent by incorporating this model as a core perception module, forming the agentic workflow for land cover change detection and analysis. GaiaAgent coordinates five task-specific agents in an automated pipeline for instruction interpretation, task decomposition, detection, and quantitative analysis. A Human-in-the-Loop mechanism is incorporated to produce interactive, interpretable reports, enhancing robustness in complex scenarios. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of GaiaAgent. On the UrbanChange dataset, GaiaAgent achieves a 3.9% improvement in F1 and a 0.35 m reduction in cRMSE compared with the strongest baseline. In downstream applications across multiple analytical scenarios, GaiaAgent demonstrates improved reliability and adaptability in land cover change detection and interpretation.

record.title: Hemispheric-scale mapping of thaw slumps using a cloud-native and transferable deep learning framework
record.abstract: Accelerating permafrost degradation is driving the rapid expansion of thaw slumps (TS) across the Northern Hemisphere, posing increasing risks to ecosystems, infrastructure, and the global carbon cycle. However, reliable TS identification at continental to hemispheric scales remains challenging due to strong environmental heterogeneity, fragmented remote sensing workflows, and limited cross-regional transferability of existing methods. Here, we address the cross-regional transferability gap in hemispheric TS identification by developing a reproducible framework that couples cloud-native multi-source data fusion in Google Earth Engine (GEE) with a modular PyTorch-based deep learning pipeline. The framework operationalizes transferability through three coordinated components: (1) a physically interpretable channel design that integrates Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and topographic data to encode TS-relevant processes; (2) a structure-preserving feature representation using PCA-guided dimensionality reduction and SNIC-based superpixel segmentation to suppress noise while maintaining geomorphic consistency; and (3) a standardized cross-regional training and ablation strategy that identifies model configurations maximizing generalization rather than region-specific accuracy. Evaluations across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), the Arctic, and the broader Northern Hemisphere demonstrate that late-summer observations and fused optical–SAR channels consistently outperform single-sensor inputs. The LinkNet-EfficientNet-B7 configuration achieves intersection-over-union (IOU) scores of 0.802 in the QTP, 0.770 in the Arctic, and 0.776 at hemispheric scale. Cross-regional transfer experiments further confirm robust generalization, with the hemispheric model maintaining IOU values exceeding 0.63 across distinct permafrost domains without region-specific retraining. These results indicate that transferable TS mapping is not primarily determined by model complexity, but by the consistency between process-informed feature representation and cross-regional training design. The proposed GEE-PyTorch framework provides a computationally efficient and reproducible foundation for operational monitoring of thaw-induced geomorphic disturbances.

record.title: Rectify-Match-Reconstruct (RMR): Framework for dense and accurate metric 3D reconstruction via neural homography alignment
record.abstract: Accurate digital representations of civil infrastructure are essential for damage prognostics, condition assessment, and remaining-life prediction. While LiDAR-based sensing can generate dense geometric models, high deployment cost and extensive post-processing limit widespread use. Image-based photogrammetry offers a scalable alternative but struggles with scale ambiguity, unreliable feature correspondence, and degraded performance under wide baselines, repetitive textures, and geometric misalignment. These limitations significantly reduce the accuracy of dense metric 3D reconstruction required for structural assessment. This paper formulates a rectify-match-reconstruct (RMR) framework for generating dense, metrically accurate 3D reconstructions from field image collections. The method is built on the key insight that correspondence errors arise primarily from severe geometric misalignment between image pairs. To address this, a self-supervised, patch-wise neural homography alignment network is developed to geometrically rectify local image regions prior to dense matching. An iterative refinement process progressively improves alignment, enabling dense correspondence estimation to operate in a stable regime even under wide-baseline viewpoints and nonplanar scene geometry. The resulting correspondences are mapped back to the original images and combined with camera calibration referenced to the Building Information Model (BIM) to achieve dense metrically consistent 3D reconstructions. Extensive validation across structures of varying scale, texture, and viewpoint separation demonstrates that RMR brings over 90% reduction in correspondence error relative to state-of-the-art optical flow methods. The framework also enables self-supervised fine-tuning of dense matching models using field imagery, further improving reconstruction accuracy. By reframing homography as a geometric preconditioning mechanism, the proposed approach provides a practical and scalable pathway toward reliable, low-cost digital twin generation and automated structural condition assessment. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tmatiki2/RMR.

record.title: T2Net: Taxonomy-Guided Tree-Structured Prompt Learning for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification
record.abstract: Remote sensing image scene classification has long faced two major challenges: high inter-class similarity and significant intra-class variation, which limit the generalization ability of Vision Language Models (VLMs) in few-shot remote sensing scene classification tasks. Existing approaches leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate additional textual descriptions, but these unstructured and generic descriptions fail to effectively address these challenges at the semantic level in complex remote sensing scenes, where rich spatial layouts and complex land-cover distributions further exacerbate intra- and inter-class variations. To address this issue, we propose Taxonomy-Guided Tree-Structured Prompt Learning for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification (T2Net). Specifically, we first introduce the Taxonomic Knowledge Generation (TKG) module, which guides LLMs to construct tree-structured semantic representations using taxonomic knowledge. The generated root- and child-level semantics are then incorporated into prompt templates via different connectives. Root nodes define macro-level semantic boundaries to enhance inter-class separability, while child nodes capture shared intra-class characteristics to reduce intra-class variation. Furthermore, we introduce a bidirectional Taxonomic Knowledge Interaction (TKI) module to enable cross-modal exchange of taxonomic knowledge. Finally, we align taxonomic-aware features with learnable prompt representations to prevent semantic drift during training. Experiments across eight public datasets demonstrate that our T2Net outperforms existing methods.

record.title: Integrating physical modeling and data-driven learning: A DCNN for InSAR phase filtering and applications
record.abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) phase filtering is crucial for stable phase unwrapping and accurate topographic mapping and deformation retrieval. However, conventional spatial, frequency, and nonlocal filters, as well as existing learning-based methods, often struggle to balance noise suppression and detail preservation, especially under extremely low coherence and high fringe density, where oversmoothing and artifacts are prone to occur. This paper proposes InSAR-Net, a deep neural network for phase filtering targeting severely noisy InSAR scenarios. The network is trained on a high-fidelity physics-based synthetic dataset that spans a wide range of coherence levels, fringe densities, and deformation patterns, with enriched extremely low-coherence samples to improve robustness. InSAR-Net integrates Feature Separation Coding (FSC) to enhance phase-related physical representations, residual dense encoding with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) for multi-scale modeling, and Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) with phase consistency loss to suppress pseudo fringes while preserving edges and fine structures. Experiments on simulated and real SAR datasets demonstrate that InSAR-Net achieves superior performance over representative SOTA methods in terms of RMSE, PSNR, and SSIM, with more pronounced gains under strong noise conditions. Further validation using low-coherence masking, detrended residual phase analysis, and unwrapped phase stability assessment shows that InSAR-Net reduces random phase fluctuations and scattering-related noise in valid coherent areas, improves phase unwrapping reliability, and avoids physical interpretation of signal-void regions. The dataset and trained model will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/yangwangyangzi48/InSAR-Net.git.

record.title: SyneFloor: Synergizing zero-shot geometric priors and active learning for weakly supervised floorplan reconstruction
record.abstract: Indoor floorplan reconstruction from 3D point clouds is a fundamental task for digital twin and architectural modeling. However, fully supervised approaches heavily rely on exhaustive polygon-level annotations, which are notoriously time-consuming and labor-intensive to acquire. To address this bottleneck, we propose SyneFloor, a weakly supervised framework that achieves accurate floorplan reconstruction under extreme label scarcity. First, to overcome the structural degradation caused by sparse supervision, we extract robust instance-aware structural priors by leveraging the zero-shot segmentation capabilities of vision foundation models (e.g., SAM3). We then propose an Adaptive Mask-Query Synergistic Fusion (AMQSF) module to dynamically fuse these explicit geometric priors into Transformer queries. Second, to maximize the data efficiency of the limited annotation budget, we design a stage-wise, multi-criteria active learning strategy. By comprehensively evaluating predictive uncertainty and architectural complexity, the model actively selects the most informative and challenging scenes for annotation. Third, to fully exploit the remaining unannotated data, we introduce a topology-aware pseudo-label generation mechanism within a dual-network collaborative framework. By explicitly detecting and resolving topological conflicts, this mechanism produces high-quality, structurally valid pseudo-labels, which fundamentally guarantees the robustness of the semi-supervised learning process. Extensive experiments on the synthetic Structured3D and real-world SceneCAD datasets demonstrate the superiority of SyneFloor. It not only exhibits robustness by consistently outperforming current state-of-the-art methods under extreme label scarcity (1% to 10% budgets), but also matches or surpasses several 100% fully supervised methods with much less labeled expenditure (e.g. utilizing only 40% of labels). This dual capability thereby establishes a highly scalable and annotation-efficient paradigm for automated indoor floorplan reconstruction in practical applications.

record.title: Arctic sea ice motion retrieval via vision foundation model and cross-sensor SAR
record.abstract: Monitoring Arctic sea ice motion (SIM) is of critical importance for polar climate research. Although synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enables all weather observations, the relatively long revisit interval of a single sensor constrains the spatial and temporal extent of SIM monitoring. Cross-sensor SAR collaboration can overcome this limitation, yet it is challenged by pronounced nonlinear radiometric distortions (NRDs) and geometric distortions between images. To address these issues, this study proposes a vision foundation model-driven framework for cross-sensor SAR collaborative monitoring of Arctic SIM. First, a cross-sensor feature extraction module via the DINOv2 vision foundation model is developed to derive robust semantic features that mitigate NRDs. Second, a multi-scale optical flow estimation module with embedded SIM Physics is designed to alleviate geometric distortions. Experiments using Sentinel-1, ALOS-2, RCM, and C-SAR data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in vector retrieval under both summer and winter conditions. Comparisons with IABP buoy measurements indicate that the retrieved velocity RMSE is within 0.73 cm/s and the directional RMSE is within 4.6°. In addition, the proposed framework substantially enhances spatiotemporal coverage, increasing the average number of effective coverage days over the Arctic by 53% and the average effective coverage area by 75%. This work provides a new technical pathway toward large scale, high precision SIM monitoring across the entire Arctic.

record.title: Advancing hyperspectral nutrient modeling through transfer learning: Insights from foliar N–P–K estimation in cranberries
record.abstract: Efficient and accurate monitoring of crop nutrient status is essential for optimizing fertilization and promoting sustainable production. Hyperspectral remote sensing offers a promising approach for estimating foliar nutrient concentrations, yet the transferability of predictive models across different spatial, temporal, and plant domains remains a major challenge. In this study, we systematically evaluated the effectiveness of transfer learning techniques for improving the transferability of hyperspectral models in predicting cranberry foliar nitrogen (Nmass), phosphorus (Pmass), and potassium (Kmass) concentrations. We assessed four transfer scenarios: (1) across geographic locations (from NEON domains to a cranberry farm in Wisconsin); (2) across growth stages; (3) across leaf types; and (4) from PROSAIL-PRO–derived synthetic datasets to field-measured datasets. Four representative transfer learning approaches — transfer component analysis (TCA), transfer adaptive boosting for regression (TrAdaBoostR2), parameter regularization, and fine-tuning — were applied to partial least squares regression (PLSR) and deep neural network (DNN) models. Results showed that baseline models trained on source domains performed poorly when directly applied to target domains, with median normalized root-mean-square-errors (nRMSE) ranging from 16 to 71 % across scenarios. Transfer learning substantially improved model performance and reduced prediction uncertainty, with parameter regularization and TrAdaBoostR2 generally outperforming TCA. Model transferability varied with nutrient type: Nmass exhibited higher temporal variability and greater distributional shifts, whereas Pmass and Kmass were more reliably predicted due to their indirect spectral correlations. Fine-tuning the DNN on as little as 10–30 % of target-domain data achieved significant improvements, highlighting the efficiency of hybrid transfer learning. Our findings provide practical insights into selecting effective transfer learning strategies for hyperspectral nutrient mapping and demonstrate the feasibility of scaling nutrient monitoring across diverse crop systems, growth stages, and leaf types.

record.title: Aerial–ground LiDAR place recognition with patch-level self-supervised learning and expanded reciprocal re-ranking
record.abstract: LiDAR place recognition determines one’s position on a prior point cloud map. The most studied ground-level LiDAR place recognition suffers from pre-visit requirements, incomplete coverage, and limited perspectives. Using pre-acquired Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS) data with broad spatial coverage as an aerial prior map overcomes these drawbacks, making cross-view place recognition necessary and advantageous. However, aerial–ground LiDAR place recognition faces a significant challenge from the domain gap between aerial and ground point clouds. Existing studies are limited by false positives in initial retrieval and the lack of large-scale benchmarks. To overcome these limitations, we present a novel retrieval and re-ranking framework for aerial–ground LiDAR place recognition. Based on the prior that neighboring point cloud patches share related semantics and geometries with the anchor patch, we select similar neighboring patches at multiple scales and aggregate their features to refine the anchor patch representation. Our retrieval network integrates these patch-level self-supervised learning modules with scene-level learning to improve the discriminativeness of global features across aerial and ground point clouds. As a self-supervised approach, it eliminates the need for manual annotations and demonstrates strong generalization. Furthermore, leveraging the structured spatial distribution of ALS point clouds, we introduce an Expanded Reciprocal (ER) re-ranking algorithm to exploit neighborhood information maximally and refine each feature based on neighbor features, which are then used to update the similarity matrix for final ranking. To evaluate our approach, we establish a new large-scale benchmark named CS-Urban-Scenes. Collected via a backpack mobile mapping system with post-processed kinematic (PPK) optimized trajectories, the dataset features an 18.1 km trajectory and a 7.2 km2 coverage area. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our retrieval network outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, achieving a 9.8% improvement in average Recall@1 and a 3.2% improvement in average Recall@1% on the CS-Urban-Scenes, while also showing the best performance on the CS-Campus3D dataset. Additionally, our ER re-ranking algorithm further boosts the average Recall@1 by 4.9% on CS-Campus3D and 10.2% on CS-Urban-Scenes without additional training.

record.title: Aerial Image Gravity Direction Estimation (AGE): Robust single-image estimation by fusing foundation model features with camera geometry
record.abstract: Estimating the gravity direction from a single aerial image provides an absolute vertical prior, which is valuable for spatial reasoning when multi-view stereo or external spatial references are unavailable. Although onboard inertial measurement units (IMUs) provide platform attitude, transferring these measurements to the camera coordinate frame requires precise synchronization and accurate extrinsic calibration, which are not always satisfied for low-cost aerial platforms. Moreover, such calibration information is often unavailable for crowdsourced or historical aerial imagery. These limitations make vision-based approaches a practical alternative for estimating gravity direction directly from images. However, reliable estimation from a single aerial image remains challenging due to the wide range of aerial viewing angles, which often leads to ambiguous geometric cues. In this work, we propose Aerial Image Gravity Direction Estimation (AGE), a framework for estimating gravity direction from a single aerial image. To resolve geometric ambiguity under diverse viewing configurations, AGE combines semantically rich features from a frozen DINOv2 backbone with camera-aware geometric features derived from known camera intrinsics. Geometric reasoning is guided by supervision from an intermediate Perspective Field, while gravity is predicted as a 3D unit vector for stable learning across aerial viewpoints. To facilitate training and evaluation, we construct AGE-Pano, a large-scale synthetic dataset containing 28,500 images with accurate ground-truth gravity directions and diverse camera viewpoints and intrinsics. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world aerial imagery demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness under aerial viewing conditions.

record.title: FICA: Fine-Grained Invariant Causal Adaptation for few-shot remote sensing scene classification
record.abstract: Remote-sensing scene classification under limited annotations and domain shifts remains challenging for Vision-language adaptation. Existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods mainly rely on global alignment or auxiliary patch-level alignment, but often lack explicit semantic guidance to enhance intra-class compactness and reduce inter-class ambiguity. To address this issue, this paper proposes FICA (Fine-Grained Invariant Causal Adaptation), a PEFT framework that explicitly integrates invariant semantic modeling with fine-grained evidence aggregation for few-shot remote-sensing scene classification. Specifically, FICA first performs invariance-oriented semantic mining to extract semantic factors that are both class-relevant and domain-stable, and then compacts them into a shared invariant subspace through SVD-based semantic grouping. The resulting subspace is injected as additional tokens into intermediate layers of CLIP, enabling feature encoding to focus on more discriminative and transferable cues. Unlike previous prompt-based patch alignment methods, FICA further uses the subspace-enhanced visual class token to adaptively select discriminative patches and generate evidence-conditioned logits, which are fused with global logits for final prediction. Experiments on base-to-new generalization, few-shot learning, and cross-dataset transfer demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms the state of the art by 5.37%, 4.34%, and 9.46%, respectively. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/yanyandadi/FICA.

record.title: CMCL-PR: Cross-modal camera-to-LiDAR place recognition with cross-attention contrastive learning
record.abstract: Place recognition is a fundamental component for robots and autonomous vehicles, enabling localization and loop closure within pre-built global maps. While single-modal approaches have achieved promising performance, cross-modal place recognition — retrieving low-cost camera images from large-scale point cloud databases — remains highly challenging due to severe modality discrepancies. In this paper, we propose CMCL-PR, a lightweight contrastive learning-based framework for image-to-point-cloud place recognition. Instead of relying on computationally expensive depth estimation or semantic segmentation, CMCL-PR introduces a perspective projection-based field-of-view (FoV) transformation to convert LiDAR point clouds into a perspective-aligned, image-like representation, thereby reducing viewpoint inconsistency between modalities. A dual-branch intra-modal encoder with shared Transformer layers is then designed to extract modality-specific features while enforcing a unified feature distribution across modalities. Furthermore, an inter-modal consistency–guided cross-attention module is introduced to explicitly model both intra-modal and inter-modal correlations, enabling the extraction of highly discriminative cross-modal descriptors. To effectively optimize the proposed architecture, a multi-objective contrastive learning strategy is adopted, which jointly incorporates cross-modal contrastive loss, intra-modal consistency loss, and matching supervision loss. Extensive experiments on three public datasets (KITTI, KITTI-360, and Oxford RobotCar) and our self-collected Snail-Radar dataset, demonstrate that CMCL-PR achieves competitive performance with real-time efficiency, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained platforms. record.title: Making Transformer interpretable by design: A self-representation architecture for multi-scenario fine-grained land cover mapping
record.abstract: Fine-grained land cover mapping leveraging deep learning and hyperspectral remote sensing imagery (HRSI) plays an important role in a wide range of application scenarios. Currently, Transformer has shown strong potential in this task due to its global modeling capability. However, despite its promising performance, the limited interpretability remains a serious concern for model reliability. To bridge this gap, we propose an inherently interpretable self-representation Transformer (SRTF) that integrates the mathematical reasoning of representation models into the Transformer architecture design. More specifically, the proposed SRTF replaces the two most opaque components in Transformer, the self-attention mechanism and the multilayer perceptron, with theoretically grounded self-representation mechanism (SRM) and class subspace learning (CSSL), respectively. First, SRM is inspired by the optimization principle of sparse representation, constructing long-range dependencies using the input itself as the dictionary. Meanwhile, to enable parallel interactions among local features, SRM is further extended to a grouped version. Second, the CSSL module is developed based on the subspace decomposition process to extract discriminative subspace components, with a fidelity loss imposed to guarantee valid decomposition. Moreover, to enhance the transparency of the decision-making process, each subspace component in the final CSPL module is explicitly associated with a specific class, enabling each decision to be traced back to its corresponding feature subspace. Experiments were conducted across multiple land cover scenarios in China, each with at least 20 fine-grained classes. Results and analyses demonstrate that the proposed SRTF, while providing enhanced interpretability, also delivers strong practical performance and consistently outperforms related methods in both accuracy and generalization capability.

record.title: Real-time deformation monitoring of long-span bridges by coupling computer vision with inertial measurement
record.abstract: Deformation monitoring of long-span bridges is essential for evaluating their structural health and safety. Traditional methods are labor-intensive and low-frequency. Image-based approaches offer precise deformation results but deteriorate with distance; thus, they cannot meet the requirements of long-span bridges. To fill these gaps, this study proposes a real-time deformation monitoring approach by integrating cameras with inertial sensors (RTDCI). Cameras capture the relative deformation of targets using computer vision. Multiple cameras are serially integrated to extend the measurement range. Inertial sensors compensate for camera motion errors alongside structural deformation. A multi-camera deformation measurement model is developed to process both images and inertial data. Laboratory and field experiments were conducted. Results demonstrate that RTDCI achieves an error of 0.32 mm with a 30 Hz frequency and 34 frames per second (FPS) in a vibrating laboratory environment. Field experiments exhibit millimeter-level accuracy when compared with hydrostatic leveling and ground-based interferometric radar. It offers an alternative deformation monitoring approach for long-span infrastructures and can be extended to complex construction environments.

record.title: Sparse weakly semi-supervised learning for oriented ship detection in polarimetric SAR images
record.abstract: A consistent trend in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) remote sensing is to reduce the dependence on dense annotations while maintaining reliable target monitoring capability in complex scenes. Sparse weakly semi-supervised learning addresses this demand by exploiting limited weak instance annotations, but its application to PolSAR ship detection remains constrained by insufficient discriminative priors, incomplete target evidence, and the loss of valuable supervisory signals. To address these issues, this paper proposes a sparse weakly semi-supervised tri-evidence recovery (SWS-TER) network for oriented ship detection. First, an annotation-free contrastive prior construction is introduced to construct region-level reliability priors by combining polarimetric superpixel region cues with momentum contrastive encoding. Second, a sparse-weak evidence completion student is designed to alleviate the over-reliance on strong local scatterers through scale adaptive context compensation and scattering keypoint graph. Third, an uncertainty-guided supervision recovery teacher is developed to transform the hard rejection of uncertain pseudo-labels into a soft semantic recovery process, preventing potentially informative samples from being discarded. Extensive experiments on the GaoFen-3 and RADARSAT − 2 images show the effectiveness of the proposed solution. SWS-TER achieves 75.5 % AP, which is 4.8 % higher than the second-best SPWOOD. As the annotation ratio further decreases, SWS-TER still achieves an AP of 60.7 % under the extremely sparse setting with less than 1 % annotations, demonstrating a more pronounced performance advantage. The G-R dataset is publicly available at https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-jJ_NxLoizAElMlTl6Aaf4Sn2zxAW-PI/view?usp=drive_link, and the code is publicly available at https://github.com/YucongHe462/SWS-TER.

record.title: Combining knowledge-based training data generation and deep learning algorithms for mapping surface water bodies, wetlands, and paddy rice in Northeast Asia
record.abstract: Annual maps of water-related land cover types, including surface water bodies, wetlands, and paddy rice, are essential for biodiversity conservation, climate regulation, food security, and infectious disease risk assessment. However, the existing large-scale data products have moderate accuracy and incomplete representation of these land cover types, and are not up to date. Moreover, those mapping approaches that rely on knowledge-based methods often suffer from insufficient good-quality observations within key phenological windows. The machine learning models are constrained by the lack of good-quality and temporally consistent training data. In this study, we proposed a two-stage mapping framework that explicitly combines knowledge-based training data generation and deep learning algorithms to leverage their complementary strengths. We first applied the established knowledge-based rules (classifiers) to produce maps of individual land cover types, which were geo-processed and filtered to generate training data. The resultant training data were used to train a deep neural network with multi-source time-series observations for classification of multiple land cover types. Using this framework, we produced a 30 m water-related land cover map for Northeast Asia in 2021, named OU-WRLC, achieving an overall accuracy of 93.8 ± 0.2%. Northeast Asia contained a total of 1,239,234 km2 of water-related land cover types, of which 17% was yearlong surface water bodies, 76% wetlands (15% seasonal open-canopy marshes and 61% yearlong closed-canopy marshes), and 7% paddy rice. The map showed strong consistency with existing products for surface water bodies and paddy rice, while providing improved spatial details. It captured extensive yearlong closed-canopy marshes that are less consistently represented in the existing datasets. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive mapping approach, supporting regional-scale environmental monitoring and land management.

record.title: Conditional diffusion model with residual decomposition generation strategy for SAR to optical image translation
record.abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)-to-optical image translation aims to recover visually interpretable optical images from SAR images acquired under all-weather and all-day conditions, yet remains challenging due to the substantial modality gap between SAR and optical image. Existing learning-based approaches exhibit complementary limitations: GAN-based methods tend to preserve global structure but often produce over-smoothed textures and suffer from training instability, while diffusion-based models excel at detail synthesis but struggle when directly modeling the full SAR-to-optical mapping, leading to structural distortions and inefficient optimization. To address these problems, this paper proposes a two-stage SAR-to-optical translation framework based on conditional residual diffusion refinement strategy (CRDRS). In the first stage, a conditional GAN generates a coarse pseudo-optical image that captures the overall scene structure, providing a stable and geometry-consistent prior. In the second stage, CRDRS is used to predict the residual between the pseudo-optical image and the real optical target, rather than directly synthesizing the optical image. CRDRS can simplify the learning objective by concentrating the diffusion process on high-frequency details and localized discrepancies. Furthermore, a heuristic theoretical analysis is provided to show that CRDRS can reduce target variance and lower intrinsic denoising error compared with direct optical generation, leading to a better conditioned optimization problem. Experiments on two representative SAR-optical datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves both pixel-level and perceptual performance, while exhibiting enhanced robustness to degraded coarse guidance. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Mizar29/Residual-Decomposition-Generation-Strategy-for-S2O.

record.title: An Adaptive Dynamic AI-driven ParameTerization (ADAPT) framework for global hourly gross primary productivity estimation
record.abstract: High-frequency estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) is crucial for understanding terrestrial carbon dynamics and ecosystem responses to rapidly changing environmental conditions. However, accurate GPP estimation at short-term timescales remains challenging, as it requires accounting for both instantaneous physiological reactions and legacy effects from antecedent environments. While light response curve (LRC) models effectively represent diurnal photosynthetic variations by capturing nonlinear light saturation, their global application has been constrained by static parameterizations. To address this, we propose the Adaptive Dynamic AI-driven ParameTerization (ADAPT) framework, which couples an LRC model with a deep learning approach. By integrating satellite-derived vegetation indices and 15-day antecedent meteorological statistics, ADAPT dynamically retrieves daily physiological parameters, enabling spatially explicit and temporally dynamic LRC parameterization. Using 328 eddy covariance flux sites globally (2001–2024), the dynamically parameterized model (LRC-DP) substantially mitigated underestimation biases associated with static models, achieving a site-level root mean squared error (RMSE) of 343.7 g C m−2 yr−1 for annual GPP. Against existing hourly products, ADAPT reduced RMSE by 25.8–32.4%, successfully reproducing midday peak productivity by overcoming the limitations of linear light-use efficiency assumptions and purely data-driven approaches. Global application at 0.05° resolution demonstrated that ADAPT captures sub-daily photosynthetic sensitivities and interannual variability consistent with global products. Highlighting its robustness under extreme climate stress, ADAPT demonstrated enhanced capability over existing products by accurately capturing daily and sub-daily GPP declines during heatwaves in the United States and Australia. This study highlights that integrating physiological mechanisms with dynamic parameterizations effectively resolves traditional scaling bottlenecks, advancing our capability to monitor high-resolution land–atmosphere carbon exchanges under climate extremes.

record.title: HELIOS-Net: Hourly daytime estimation of land surface temperature with integration of observational solar-cloud-satellite geometry and deep neural network
record.abstract: Geostationary satellite-based land surface temperature (LST) is vital for monitoring diurnal thermal dynamics owing to its extensive spatial coverage and high temporal resolution. However, frequent cloud cover results in substantial data gaps, limiting its practical utility for reliable thermal monitoring applications. The solar-cloud-satellite geometry (SCSG) effect has recently been introduced to reflect direct cloud radiative effects in LST reconstruction, but its application has been largely limited to polar-orbiting satellites. To address this limitation, we propose HELIOS-Net, a deep learning (DL) framework for hourly daytime LST reconstruction using the GEO-KOMPSAT-2A satellite across South Korea, central Japan, and southeastern Australia. The framework combines SCSG-based regime partitioning with a generative adversarial network (GAN) to reconstruct spatially continuous all-sky LST by leveraging satellite observations and various meteorological and topographic variables. Validation against in-situ observations demonstrated that HELIOS-Net achieved high performance across all regions, with coefficient of determination (R2) values of 0.63–0.94 and root mean square error (RMSE) values of 2.45–7.65 °C under cloudy-sky conditions. Comparative evaluation further indicated an overall performance advantage over ERA5-Land and an existing all-sky LST product derived from satellite observations. Additional analyses confirmed that both the SCSG effect and the DL framework contribute to enhancing the fidelity of hourly daytime LST reconstruction. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework to enable high-quality, spatially continuous all-sky LST monitoring from geostationary satellites, providing a promising approach mitigating cloud-induced data gaps under diverse viewing geometries and environmental conditions.

record.title: Clinical readiness of foundation and agentic AI in computational pathology
record.abstract: Foundation and agentic AI show great promise for computational pathology, with clinical readiness now widely anticipated. We define readiness at the intended-use system level; outline requirements for evidence, validation, economic sustainability, and governance; and propose a roadmap toward responsible deployment.

record.title: BiCoA-Net: An Interpretable Bidirectional Co-Attention Framework for Predicting Protein-Ligand Binding Kinetics
record.abstract: A quantitative understanding of protein-ligand binding kinetics, particularly the dissociation rate constant (koff), is fundamental to characterizing the dynamics of molecular recognition and optimizing in vivo pharmacodynamics. However, predicting koff from molecular data remains a central challenge due to complex unbinding transition states and persistent data scarcity. Here, we confront these challenges by first curating KinetX, the largest comprehensive benchmark dataset of experimental koff values to date, comprising 5,624 measurements across 256 distinct protein targets. We then introduce BiCoA-Net, an interpretable deep learning framework designed to model reciprocal physicochemical interactions from sequence representations. The model employs a bidirectional co-attention mechanism and an adaptive gated fusion layer to learn these complex, non-linear interactions. BiCoA-Net achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and shows strong generalization in cold-start scenarios, where protein targets are novel. Furthermore, the model's interpretability features identify key physicochemical descriptors and reveal bimodal interaction strategies. Validation on four held-out, clinically relevant targets confirms its practical utility, demonstrating robust compound ranking and significant enrichment in virtual screening tasks. BiCoA-Net and KinetX provide a robust, generalizable, and interpretable framework for the computational prediction and optimization of drug-target binding kinetics

record.title: Towards resolution-arbitrary remote sensing change detection with Spatial-frequency dual domain learning
record.abstract: Deep learning-based change detection (CD) is widely used for same-resolution images. However, high-resolution remote sensing images are often not continuously available over time, necessitating the ability to handle images with arbitrary resolution differences. Previous super-resolution (SR)-assisted CD methods are limited to processing bi-temporal images with fixed resolution differences and fail to adequately preserve edges. Moreover, existing CD methods ignore the potential of frequency domain analysis for difference features. To address these limitations, this article proposes a novel resolution-arbitrary CD network that enables CD with input images of arbitrary resolution differences. The framework is distinctive because it can solve resolution mismatch and boost accuracy by enabling high- and low-level tasks (i.e., CD and arbitrary scale SR) to learn from each other. A gradient-enhanced magnification-arbitrary module is designed to resize input images to a uniform size while preserving edge details better. Furthermore, unlike existing methods that solely consider difference features in spatial domain, a difference dual-domain learning module is designed to capture global contextual and local information from difference features in the spatial and frequency domains, improving the change representation. Experiments on four datasets including real and simulated data demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in handling arbitrary resolution differences. The codes are available at https://github.com/LYT-max/RACDNet.

record.title: MHFNet: Multimodal hybrid fusion framework for misaligned SAR-Optical ship detection
record.abstract: Multimodal ship detection using optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is highly desirable for robust maritime monitoring. However, most existing fusion-based methods assume spatially aligned optical–SAR pairs, an assumption that rarely holds in practice due to differences in sensor geometry, acquisition timing, and registration errors. Such misalignment severely undermines the effectiveness of conventional fusion strategies. To address this challenge, we propose MHFNet, an alignment-aware hybrid fusion framework that systematically integrates improvements at the feature, loss, and decision levels. First, we introduce a Feature Alignment and Fusion Module (FAFM) that leverages deformable convolution and content-guided attention to achieve robust cross-modal feature alignment. Second, we design an Uncertainty-Aware Shape IoU Loss (US-Loss) that downweights unreliable training samples caused by cross-modal label shift while enhancing bounding box regression with shape-aware constraints. Third, we develop a Distance Matching Probabilistic Fusion (DMP-Fusion) algorithm that resolves inconsistencies in multimodal detection outputs through distance-based matching and Bayesian inference. Extensive experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets (QXS and Suez) show that MHFNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, improving average precision by up to + 4.77 % and F1-score by + 4.93 %. These results demonstrate that MHFNet offers a robust and generalizable solution to multimodal ship detection under realistic cross-modal misalignment conditions. The code and datasets are released on https://github.com/wsdmw1/MHFNet.

record.title: Switcher-HNet: A switchable hierarchical network for tree species classification from forest stand to individual tree tasks
record.abstract: Tree species information is essential for effective forest management, ecosystem health, and species biodiversity. Currently, most classification models treat tree species as independent categories and overlook the hierarchical relationships among these species, hindering the accuracy and effectiveness of tree species classification. To address this issue, this study proposes Switcher-HNet, a switchable hierarchical convolutional network integrating a backbone network, a hierarchical module, and a switcher mechanism to leverage tree species hierarchies and enhance their identification. This study introduces two hierarchical datasets structured at three levels: land cover (level 0), foliage type (level 1), and tree species (level 2). The TreeSatAI dataset, collected in Germany, is designed for forest stand classification with dominant species such as pine, beech, spruce, and oak. The Hierarchical Individual Tree (HIT) dataset, acquired in northeastern China, targets individual tree classification and is primarily composed of Pinus koraiensis and various broadleaf species. These two datasets provide a structured label hierarchy and a multi-scale perspective across biogeographically distinct regions. SENet, the top-performing backbone among the evaluated networks, was selected as the shared backbone for both Switcher-HNet and a hierarchical baseline on these datasets. Results show that Switcher-HNet outperformed the baseline on the TreeSatAI dataset, achieving a 0.89% improvement in overall accuracy (OA) at level 1 and a significant 2.95% increase at level 2. To evaluate transferability, Switcher-HNet, pretrained on the TreeSatAI dataset, was fine-tuned on the HIT dataset for individual tree classification. Switcher-HNet achieved high accuracy with OAs of 94.00% at level 1 and 90.59% at level 2 on the full HIT dataset, reducing training time to less than one-third of that required for training from scratch. Therefore, the fine-tuning techniques enable a smooth transition from forest stand to individual tree classification. This study emphasizes the potential of hierarchical classification methods to enhance tree species identification and provides a technical support for sustainable forest management and biodiversity conservation.

record.title: UnravelNet: A backbone for enhanced multi-scale and low-quality feature extraction in remote sensing object detection
record.abstract: Remote sensing object detection (RSOD) faces significant challenges, including substantial variations in object sizes within a single image and the presence of low-quality object features. Previous approaches have attempted to mitigate these issues by employing large spatial receptive fields, such as through large kernel convolutions, or by using multi-scale convolutional kernels to capture features from objects of varying sizes. However, large kernel convolutions often fail to extract detailed object features effectively, while multi-scale convolutional kernels struggle to capture relevant features of low-quality or blurry objects, leading to reduced detection accuracy. To address these issues, this study presents UnravelNet, a novel backbone network tailored for RSOD. UnravelNet innovatively disentangles the coupling of multi-scale features through a non-expansive multi-branch attention mechanism, incorporating point, local and mid-range attention. Additionally, UnravelNet improves the representation of low-quality features by integrating edge information and Gaussian distributions. This approach enables UnravelNet to efficiently utilize a limited number of parameters while effectively extracting both multi-scale and low-quality features. Extensive experiments on standard RSOD benchmarks demonstrate the superior performance of UnravelNet, achieving state-of-the-art results with mAPs of 79.99% on DOTA-v1.0, 73.09% on DOTA-v1.5, 69.48% on DIOR-R and 44.44% on FAIR1M-v1.0. These results highlight the improvements in both accuracy and efficiency for RSOD tasks, underscoring the potential of UnravelNet as a robust solution for remote sensing applications. The code will be available at https://github.com/lwCVer/UnravelNet.

record.title: Bias-aware learning for unbiased scene graph generation in remote sensing imagery
record.abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) in remote sensing imagery (RSI) plays a critical role in advancing the understanding of geospatial scenarios. The incorporation of scene graphs, which capture the relationships between objects within imagery, has significantly enhanced the performance of various RS tasks, such as RS image retrieval and RS image captioning. However, the long-tailed distribution of relationships has adversely affected the SGG quality, leading to biased relationship predictions. In our previous Sample-Level Bias Prediction (SBP) method, we find that the union region of one object pair (i.e., one sample) contains rich and dedicated contextual information, enabling the prediction of the sample-specific bias for correcting the biased relationship prediction. Nevertheless, SBP employs a single model to correct all categories, which results in the suppression of certain relationship categories while enhancing the detection accuracy of others. To address this challenge, we present a Bias-Aware Learning (BAL) method that employs group collaboration to alleviate the burden of a single model correcting all categories. During BAL, we initially group the relationship categories and deploy group-specific SBP models to learn and predict the corresponding biases within their relationships. Subsequently, we design a Group-Collaborative Distillation (GCD) strategy to facilitate the collaboration among SBP models from different groups, thereby alleviating category suppression and enhancing the overall performance of SGG. The extensive experimental results on STAR and AUG datasets for RSI demonstrate that our BAL outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. Compared to the best model RPCM on STAR, RPCM equipped with BAL shows a significant average improvement of 5.08%/5.00%, 3.87%/3.64% and 0.22%/0.25% on HMR@K for PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet tasks, respectively. Moreover, we have also validated the effectiveness and generalization of our BAL on VG dataset for natural imagery. The code will be available at https://github.com/Zhuzi24/BAL.

record.title: Compact-pol to quad-pol SAR reconstruction via a joint mathematical-physical-constrained multimodal correlation-preserving latent diffusion framework
record.abstract: Compact-polarimetric (CP) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers wide swath coverage and relatively rich polarimetric information, making it a promising mode of earth observation. However, compared to quad-polarimetric (QP) data, CP data are still limited in fully characterizing polarimetric scattering mechanisms. Existing methods for reconstructing QP data from CP data face challenges such as the lack of physical properties in the QP covariance matrix and insufficient utilization of polarimetric, terrain, and imaging information. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multimodal correlation-preserving latent diffusion framework under mathematical-physical constraints for CP to QP SAR data reconstruction (SAR-C2QM). First, we propose a mathematical-physical hard constraint through the Cholesky decomposition method and a two-dimensional phase vector encoding approach, ensuring both the positive semi-definiteness and phase continuity of the reconstructed QP data. Next, SAR image modality and corresponding terrain-imaging information modality are constructed based on multi-source data, providing rich polarimetric and effective terrain-imaging multimodal information for model training. Furthermore, a multimodal correlation-preserving latent diffusion model with a hierarchical bidirectional cross-attention module is designed, enabling the fusion of multimodal and multi-scale features, with mathematical-physical constraints guiding the reconstruction process to achieve high-fidelity QP reconstruction across large-area coverage and complex terrain conditions. Experiments on simulated CP data derived from Gaofen-3 and Radarsat-2 QP data across diverse wave codes demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and stability. Specifically, the Wishart distance error between reconstructed and original QP data is reduced by over 12.1%. Moreover, the overall accuracy of land cover classification using the reconstructed QP data improves by an average of 15.1% compared to CP data, closely approaching the classification accuracy of the original QP data. The code is available in https://github.com/zihuan21/SAR-C2QM.

record.title: EAME: Element-Aware Multi-UAV distributed autonomous exploration for efficient and complete under-canopy measurements
record.abstract: Multi-UAV collaborative exploration systems have demonstrated significant potential in mapping, and search-and-rescue operations. However, current multi-UAV collaborative exploration approaches still face substantial challenges in achieving safe, efficient, and complete autonomous surveying and mapping in complex environments, such as under-canopy scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper introduces EAME, an Element-Aware Multi-UAV distributed Exploration strategy. First, we propose an element-aware frontier classification and adaptive viewpoint generation method, which identifies the potential element information in the environment through reasonable frontier classification, and generates high-quality viewpoints according to different frontier types, guiding the UAV to quickly cover the unknown space while collecting complete elements’ data. Then, based on the set of viewpoints generated in the previous step, a hybrid-hierarchical planning approach is introduced, adopting different planning approaches to generate both global and local trajectories tailored to specific targets, thus effectively improving trajectory quality. Finally, a greedy workload reallocation strategy is designed to minimize unnecessary maneuvers by some UAVs during the later stages of exploration, thereby reducing system energy consumption. Extensive tests were conducted in environments with varying obstacle densities, and the results demonstrate that the proposed EAME outperforms existing methods in terms of exploration efficiency, element coverage, and number of collisions.

record.title: Physically-constrained flow learning reveals diurnal submesoscale surface currents from geostationary satellite observations
record.abstract: Submesoscale processes (length scales of 0.1–10 km) play a critical role in oceanic energy dissipation and mass transport, yet traditional satellite altimetry data—with coarse spatial (∼25 km) and temporal (daily) resolution—are insufficient to resolve its dynamics. Geostationary satellite ocean-color imagers such as GOCI-II can observe hourly at 250 m resolution, but the filament-rich evolution of surface tracers complicates current inference from image sequences. Here, we develop the BAPDE-RAFT, a boundary-aware, Poisson-based, near-divergence-free–constrained extension of the RAFT optical-flow network, to retrieve pixel-scale sea surface velocities from consecutive images, effectively estimating a physically regularized, nondivergent (rotational) component of the surface flow. Compared with the standard maximum cross-correlation (MCC) approach, BAPDE-RAFT lowers end-point and angular errors by 44 % and 38 %, respectively. Wavenumber analysis places the critical scale at which model error exceeds signal at λc ≈ 4.0 km—over an order of magnitude finer than the 60–80 km limits of traditional MCC algorithm, confirming that only BAPDE-RAFT retains spectral power throughout the 1–10 km sub-mesoscale processes. When applied to hourly GOCI-II chlorophyll-a images in the Japan Sea/East Sea, the model reproduces diurnal current variability and the expected dual cascade: an upscale kinetic-energy flux (∼k−3) and a downscale tracer cascade (∼k−1). We note that the near-divergence-free constraint may damp strongly convergent/divergent ageostrophic motions; nevertheless, despite being affected by cloud coverage, these results demonstrate that high-cadence geostationary satellite ocean color observations can yield physically consistent maps of fine-scale surface currents, opening new avenues for satellite studies of ocean dynamics and mass transport at fine scale.

record.title: SAR-NanoShipNet: A scale-adaptive network for robust small ship detection in SAR imagery
record.abstract: Currently, notable progress has been attained in small ship target detection for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, with such advancements being driven by three key methodological innovations within the deep learning framework: self-supervision combined with knowledge distillation, rotated bounding box detection, and multi-scale feature fusion. However, it still faces challenges such as high speckle noise in SAR images, difficulty in extracting small target features, geometric distortion of ship shapes and heading dependence. Therefore, this article proposes a new SAR-NanoShipNet model. To enhance the targeting of ship objects, the proposed method employs a specialized convolution (DABConv) that exhibits greater suitability for ship targets, replacing the conventional standard convolution. As opposed to traditional approaches for SAR target detection, which typically lack the capability to adaptively capture the irregular boundaries and low-contrast features of small ship targets in SAR images, this method pioneers the adaptive capture of these features through deformable convolutions and boundary attention mechanisms, leading to enhanced target localization accuracy. In addition, we introduce the VerticalCompSPPF module (VC-SPPF), which incorporates longitudinal multi-scale convolution alongside a channel attention mechanism. Finally, the design of D-CLEM is linked with DABConv to enhance directional feature extraction while also fusing, improving the accuracy of small object detection. We have validated the superiority of our method on five datasets, particularly for high precision detection of small targets (APs ↑2.66%). Our code can be found at https://github.com/Z-Yuhao/1.git.

record.title: Automated TLS multi-scan registration in forest environments: A novel solution based on hash table
record.abstract: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) has proven to be an effective tool for forest inventories due to its accurate, non-destructive capability to document 3D space structures. The multi-scan mode of TLS enables comprehensive data acquisition, but the point cloud of each scan must be aligned to a common coordinate frame. In practice, the most common solution involves manually placing artificial markers in the field, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Consequently, the automated multi-scan registration method is highly appreciated for subsequent applications. This study presents an automated TLS multi-scan registration algorithm for forest point clouds, HashReg, utilizing the high-efficiency operations of Hash Table. HashReg comprises four key procedures, including stem mapping, estimating coarse transformation parameters, factor graph optimization, and fine-tuned registration. Using optimized transformation parameters, the global poses of individual TLS scans are subsequently determined within a unified coordinate system through a depth-first strategy. Extensive experiments were performed on four datasets with diverse forest characteristics, such as dense and sparse stems, flat and undulating terrain, and natural and plantation forests. The experimental results demonstrate that HashReg achieves milliradian-level rotation accuracy and centimeter-level translation accuracy, i.e., 0–3 mrad and 0–3 cm for most of the plots, respectively. Another evaluation metric, the point-wise upper bound errors, is reported to show the variation of point discrepancy with increasing distance. For most plots, these errors remained within the centimeter range, i.e., 1–4 cm, 1–5 cm, and 2–7 cm for the distance at 5 m, 10 m, and 20 m respectively. Moreover, the efficiency of HashReg’s four key procedures was also assessed. The running time of coarse registration and global optimization is at the millisecond level, i.e., 4 ms and 6 ms, while the stem mapping and fine registration were at the second level, i.e., 3 s and 15 s. Comparison with four state-of-the-art (SOTA) point cloud registration approaches, including FMP + BnB, HL-MRF, GlobalMatch, and SGHR, was quantitatively conducted on three public datasets. HashReg achieves superior accuracy, i.e., ranking first or second across all plots, with 100 % successful registrations. It also has substantially higher efficiency, with runtime improvements exceeding two-fold relative to the SOTA methods. All these advantages demonstrate that HashReg can bridge the gap between raw data and practical applications. The implementation of HashReg is open-sourced at https://github.com/MSpace-WHU/Forest_TLS_Reg.

record.title: Synthetic learning for primitive-based building model reconstruction from point clouds
record.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital 3D environments has significantly increased the demand for geometrically accurate and semantically rich parametric building models. However, existing primitive- or model-based building reconstruction approaches often struggle with limited availability of labeled datasets and insufficient reconstruction accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a novel learning-based method for building reconstruction from point clouds that leverages roof primitives and relies exclusively on synthetic data for supervision. Our approach begins with the generation of a large synthetic dataset comprising 100,000 buildings of varying scales based on a predefined library of 10 roof primitive classes. The synthetic point clouds are created by randomly sampling not only the interiors but also the edges and corners of the roof primitives. Two lightweight transformer-based neural networks are then trained to classify roof primitive classes and estimate their corresponding parameters. Compared to conventional learning-free fitting methods, our learning-based approach achieves higher parameter estimation accuracy and greater robustness when applied to six real-world point cloud datasets collected from drone, airborne, and spaceborne platforms. Notably, the synthetic learning approach reduces primitive parameter estimation errors from approximately 50% to 6% of the point ground spacing — demonstrating a distinctive advantage when trained effectively on synthetic data. Future work may explore generating synthetic data for irregular, complex buildings, expanding the library with additional roof primitive classes, and applying the proposed training strategy to such synthetic datasets.

record.title: Roof-aware indoor BIM reconstruction from LiDAR via graph-attention for residential buildings
record.abstract: Building Information Models (BIMs) provide structured, parametric representations that are fundamental for simulation, facility management, and digital twin applications. However, reconstructing BIMs from terrestrial LiDAR scans remains challenging due to clutter, occlusions, and the geometric complexity of roof structures. This paper presents a roof-aware scan-to-BIM pipeline tailored for residential buildings, which processes indoor LiDAR data through four geometric abstractions, raw points, superpoints, triangle meshes, and volumetric polyhedra, each represented by task-specific graphs. The pipeline integrates three modules: LGNet for semantic segmentation, QTNet for floor plan reconstruction, and PPO for roof–floor fusion. It demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalization, being trained on Structured3D and fine-tuned on the real-world WHUTS dataset. The method produces watertight, Revit-compatible BIMs with an average surface deviation of 9 mm RMS on WHUTS scenes featuring slanted roofs. Compared with state-of-the-art scan-to-BIM and floor plan reconstruction methods, the proposed approach achieves higher geometric accuracy on scenes with slanted roofs, reducing surface reconstruction error by over 12–18% and improving layout reconstruction F1-scores by up to 6–8%. The proposed framework provides a robust, accurate, and fully automated solution for roof-aware BIM reconstruction of residential buildings from terrestrial LiDAR data, offering comprehensive support for slanted roof modeling. The source code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/Wangbohan-x/roof-aware-scan2bim.git.

record.title: MARSNet: A Mamba-driven adaptive framework for robust multisource remote sensing image matching in noisy environments
record.abstract: Semi-dense matching of multi-source remote sensing images under noise interference remains a challenging task. Existing detector-free methods often exhibit low efficiency and reduced performance when faced with large viewpoint variations and significant noise disturbances. Due to the inherent noise and modality differences in multi-source remote sensing images, the accuracy and robustness of feature matching are substantially compromised. To address this issue, we propose a hybrid network for multi-source remote sensing image matching based on an efficient and robust Mamba framework, named MARSNet. The network achieves efficient and robust matching through the following innovative designs: First, it leverages the efficient Mamba network to capture long-range dependencies within image sequences, enhancing the modeling capability for complex scenes. Second, a frozen pre-trained DINOv2 foundation model is introduced as a robust feature extractor, effectively improving the model’s noise resistance. Finally, an adaptive fusion strategy is employed to integrate features, and the Mamba-like linear attention mechanism is adopted to refine the Transformer-based linear attention, further enhancing the efficiency and expressive power for long-sequence processing. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, extensive experiments were conducted on multi-source remote sensing image datasets, covering various scenarios such as noise-free, additive random noise, and periodic stripe noise. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant improvements in matching accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, by performing pose error evaluation on a large-scale general dataset, the superior performance of the proposed method in 3D reconstruction is validated, complementing the test results from the multi-source remote sensing dataset, thereby providing a more comprehensive assessment of the method’s generalization ability and robustness.
